title: screener channel — schema-first (AFB backend<->AFB frontend only; not part of afb.execution.v1 wire)
description: Negotiated via auth.support/auth_ok.support (capability id afbws.screener.channel.v1). Read-only access to the screener's published JSON exports (contract v1, see AFB/docs/SCREENER_RESULTS.md); the backend never opens the screener database. Same convention as afbws.market/afbws.config: ONE schema id per message (`afbws.screener.<op>.v1`, no .request/.response suffixes); the same schema is the request and its response. `request_id` is required in every client request. The only server push is `afbws.screener.participants.v1` without `request_id` (see its description); the other operations are answered on demand. A failed request is answered with `afbws.screener.error.v1`. Operations: `list` (available exports, newest first, content not read), `get` (one export by id) and `participants` (market participants snapshot: four lists now/d1/d2/w1 of derivatives with fiz/yur positions, open interest and volume, computed by the backend from market_cache). Export ids: `night:YYYY-MM-DD` (night result of a trading day), `intraday:YYYY-MM-DDTHHMM` (intraday snapshot), or the aliases `latest` (newest night export) and `intraday_latest` (newest intraday snapshot). Access requires the `screener` capability of the user's role; otherwise `forbidden`. The exported document is intentionally an open object: only `contract_version` is relied upon; the screener's fields (signals, reliability, models, errors) evolve and are described in AFB/docs/SCREENER_RESULTS.md. A document with an unsupported `contract_version` is answered with `unsupported_action`. See AFB/docs/ws/screener.md.

exportId.description: Concrete export id: `night:YYYY-MM-DD` or `intraday:YYYY-MM-DDTHHMM` (trading day and MSK moment, no separators in the time).

exportRef.description: Export id or alias: `latest` (newest night export) / `intraday_latest` (newest intraday snapshot).

asof.description: Moment of the export's signals (MSK, no zone), derived from the file name; `night`: 19:00 of trading_day.

generated_at.description: File modification time (ISO 8601 with zone); the content is not read for the list.

list.title: afbws.screener.list.v1 — available exports (request / response).
list.description: Request carries only optional filters. Response carries `items` (newest first) and the ids of the newest exports: `latest` (newest night export) and `intraday_latest` (newest intraday snapshot), each null when there is none. Both are computed from file names, not from the screener's latest*.json copies.

kind.description: Request: only exports of this kind.

limit.description: Request: at most this many newest items.

get.title: afbws.screener.get.v1 — one export (request / response).
get.description: Request carries `id` (export id or alias). Response echoes the concrete `id` (aliases resolved) and `kind`, and carries `document`: the export content as is (contract v1), an open object. Unknown export: error `not_found`; malformed id: `invalid_schema`; unreadable file: `internal_error`; unsupported `contract_version`: `unsupported_action`.

id.description: Request: export id or alias. Response: concrete export id.

document.description: Response only. Screener export content as is; see AFB/docs/SCREENER_RESULTS.md.

favoriteColor.description: Same list and order as afbws.instrument.channel.v2 favoriteColor (kept in lockstep; no cross-reference on purpose).

participantsCollection.description: Root catalog collection (color source for the bubbles).

participantsDerivatives.description: Derivative reference table (columnar, like afbws.market.series.v1 tables): `columns` start with `derivative` (e.g. `MISX:Si`) and may list any subset of the other fields; read by column name. `name`; `active_instrument_key` = nearest unexpired contract (to open a chart); `collection_id` references `collections[].id` (null = no collection). Shared by all four lists.

rows.description: Each row has the same length and order as `columns`; a missing value is null (never NaN).

participantsList.description: One snapshot. `rows` are columnar (`columns` begin with `derivative`; the other columns are a subset of the fiz_/yur_ position fields, openinterest and volume). Only derivatives that have data in this snapshot get a row; the rest are absent (join with `derivatives` by key). `source`: `intraday` if at least one row is the intraday slot of the day, otherwise `daily`. `price` = price of the derivative's active contract (`derivatives.active_instrument_key`): the last quote for `now` when `trading_day` is today, otherwise the close of the last 5-minute slot of `trading_day`; null when there is no price. The same contract is used in all four lists, so price changes between lists are comparable.

key.description: now = latest trading day that has started (the current session once it has data, otherwise the previous trading day's close); d1 = close of the trading day before `now`; d2 = the one before d1; w1 = last trading day <= (`now` day - 7 calendar days).

asof.description: Moment of the values (MSK, no zone); for `now` the intraday slot.

rows.description: Each row has the same length and order as `columns`; a missing value is null (never NaN).

participants.title: afbws.screener.participants.v1 — market participants snapshot (request / response).
participants.description: Request is an empty command (no parameters in this version; `request_id` is required). Response carries `received_at`, `tz`, `collections`, `derivatives` (reference table) and `lists` (four columnar snapshots: now, d1, d2, w1). Server push: after each refresh of the FORTS positions (about every 5 minutes) the backend sends the same message with the full body and WITHOUT `request_id` to every connection that has requested `participants` at least once; there is no unsubscribe, the subscription ends with the connection. Access: tier `manager` or `user`, otherwise `forbidden`. Non-manager sees only derivatives visible to their tier.

tz.description: Response only. Time zone of asof, e.g. Europe/Moscow.

error.title: afbws.screener.error.v1 — typed error for a whole request (server -> client).
